supported: OCR execution and exact/CER evaluation are reproducible with two pinned backends.
A constrained clean EXP date-code format reaches 95.11% EasyOCR and 99.56% Tesseract exact-read.
not_supported: Arbitrary alphanumeric serial OCR upper bound.
Real industrial camera, lens, CIJ/laser font, or motion upper bound.
Mixed FUNSD camera-condition fields remain low: 13.04% EasyOCR and 33.33% Tesseract train-best exact.
p0_ocr_upper_bound.decision: Freeze one real target format before formal E0; current evidence favors a constrained date/batch-code task over arbitrary serial numbers.

supported: Synthetic affine instrument recovery reduced Stokes RMSE from 0.01147 to 0.00260.
PDD 120-condition audit demonstrated explicit MPFA reconstruction and AoLP sensitivity.
SHDocs 800-capture pair-sum and S0 consistency audit passed for result-level proxy use.
not_supported: Physical calibration of the future project camera.
Absolute AoLP zero point, dark/flat response, extinction ratio, or temperature drift.

status_history.superseded_because: A noise-only null reproduces a large share of the oracle gap, so the gap alone does not show complementary polarization content (see extension_controls).

extension_controls.replication: The new pipeline reproduces the first-round raw-channel E2 numbers above with zero absolute difference (both backends).

dense_fixed_angle.result: 36 synthesized virtual angles do not beat raw I0 as a fixed input (Tesseract -0.97 pp, EasyOCR -0.39 pp; intervals include 0), so the fixed baseline was not underestimated.
dense_fixed_angle.caveat: Best-of-36 oracle gap grows to +14.41 pp (Tesseract) and +5.71 pp (EasyOCR); gap rises with the number of candidates and a narrow 5-degree window already gives 67% / 47% of the 45-degree-spacing gain, so gap alone cannot separate more content from more draws.
dense_fixed_angle.per_condition_best_angle: No evidence that the best angle switches with condition: per-condition minus global fixed is -0.19 pp [-1.05, +0.76] (Tesseract), +0.58 pp [-0.48, +1.55] (EasyOCR).

e3_intensity_matching.result: Histogram matching keeps 85% (Tesseract) of the raw oracle gap and enlarges it on EasyOCR (+3.87 vs +2.51 pp, because the fixed baseline falls); mean/std matching leaves it unchanged. Global brightness/contrast is not the main source.
e3_intensity_matching.caveat: Excludes only a brightness/contrast explanation; it cannot separate spatially different glare structure from OCR instability under small perturbations.

noise_only_null.definition: Clean I0 plus three noisy re-draws of the same content (4 independent realizations per dose, PDD-High-calibrated heteroscedastic noise); best-of gain versus clean I0, same form as the real fixed gain.
noise_only_null.interpretation: The oracle gap is not, by itself, evidence of complementary polarization content. Anchored on pixel distance, Tesseract's real gap exceeds the null with a CI that excludes 0 (also on all 50 documents), which is compatible with some real content effect; EasyOCR's does not on the test split. Anchored on alternative-input readability the null explains most of the gap on the test split. The two anchors disagree, so neither 'fully explained' nor 'not explained' is supported.
noise_only_null.data_quality: 285 of 336,780 Tesseract calls (0.085%) crashed with SIGFPE, deterministically on retry and concentrated at large noise; scored as failed reads, with a drop-crashed-samples sensitivity analysis that leaves the conclusion unchanged (EasyOCR: none).

supported: The raw four-direction oracle gap repeats across two OCR backends with document-cluster CIs above zero.
All four canonical directions uniquely recover some test samples (a pattern a noise-only null can also produce).
SDK deglared, min, median, and S0 do not remove the oracle gap.
Continuous fixed virtual angles do not beat raw I0; no evidence that the best fixed angle switches with condition.
not_supported: That the oracle gap shows complementary polarization content: a same-content noise-only null reproduces about 36-72% (pixel-distance anchor) to 78-126% (post-hoc readability anchor) of it on the test split.
A deployable selector that captures the oracle gap.
Real repeated-exposure null (needs hardware); the injected-noise null cannot model correlated sensor noise or re-capture variability.
Industrial spray-code, curved material, source-polarization, or dynamic-line generalization.
p2_fixed_direction_necessity.decision: Retain adaptive polarization as a research hypothesis that is neither established nor refuted. Replace the oracle gap by a real repeated-exposure null (same scene, polarization unchanged) as the discriminating experiment once hardware is available; do not train a learned representation until task-specific E0 and that control are in hand.
